Broiler Salad No ordinary salad, sir!  Crisp Romaine leaves, watercress, tomatoes, green peppers, cucumbers, and green onions, with our own dressing of pure olive oil, wine vinegar, herbs and spices.  Per Person

Avocado Salad, with Crab or Shrimp A meal in itself.  Rich, ripe California avocado slices surround while Dungeness crab legs or Pacific prawns.  Garnished with tomatoes, sweet red onions, green pepper rings, cucumbers, hard boiled eggs and olives
Canlis' Seafood Salad a la Louis A favorite in The City renowned for its love of seafood.  Ours is a delightful symphony of crab, stuffed lobster, Pacifid prawns, and fresh vegetables

SHRIMP CANLIS  Delicious shrimp shipped essentially to us...Sauteed in a tantalizing blend of butter, olive oil, wine and garlic.
Beef Teriyaki - Slices of thin steak marinated in the traditional Japanese manner.  Served with oriental style white rice
PACIFIC MAHIMAHI  Don't let that name perplex you.  That's the Hawaiin name for one of the Islands' greatest sport fish - the unquestioned seafood favorite of gourmets.  We broil it over hardwood charcoal and season it with a tantalizing butter sauce.
Steak Tartare, Canlis - As a Main Course.  Chilled Raw Fresh Ground Beef prepared like no other Tartare Steak.
Steak Pierre - Thin slices of Filet Mignon, sauteed in butter, herbs and vermouth, with the Canlis touch.  Served with rice pilaff.
DUNGENESS CRAB LEGS.  Selected, moist crab legs sauteed in butter and lemon, served with straw potatoes and our special Tartare Sauce.
WHOLE BROILED LOBSTER TAIL.  Spectacular shellfish, these-steeped in wine, broiled and seasoned with a hot butter sauce that will pique your curiousity as well as your appetite.
Calf's Liver Steak, French Fried Onions - A prime favorite in every gourmet center of the world - the tenderest, most nutritious cut of meat in the world.  Tempting, tasty calf's liver served under a blanket of succulent French fried onions.
Jumbo Scallops en Brochette - Large tender Scallops - charcoal broiled, seasoned with our lemon butter sauce.  Flown to us fresh, in season.
SAN FRANCISTO PETRALE SOLE  San Francisco Petrale Sole, sauteed in butter, with white wine and lemon.  Served only when fresh, as available.
RAINBOW TROUT, Charcoal Broiled.  Fresh Boneless Whole Rainbow Trout, charcoal broiled and seasoned with our lemon butter sauce and served with straw potatoes.  Not from the sea, of course, but always fresh.
Jumbo Scallopes, Amandine - Suateed with melted butter and almonds.  Flown to us fresh, as available.
Fresh Broiled Salmon - Fresh salmon, obtained locally or flown in from the East or Northwest, broiled over the open hearth and seasoned with lemon butter.  As available
QUILCENE OYSTERS.  No ordinary oysters, these!  Flown to us from the cold waters of Quilcene Bay, these oysters are raised with loving care.  They are sauteed and served with straw potatoes.  Always fresh, always available.
Fresh Poached Salmon, Hollandaise - Gently poached and served with Canlis' special Hollandaise.  Served only when fresh
PACIFIC SNAPPER.  Fresh, flaky Pacific snapper caught off the coast and brought direclty to us.  We broil it over hardwood charcoal embers and basted it with butter and lemon.  Served only when fresh, as available.
Sand Dabs, Amandine - A Bay Area delicacy served only when fresh, as available.  Sauteed in butter, with white wine and almonds
Filet Mignon
Whole Milk-fed Squab, Wild Rice - A tender, plump bird, fairly bursting with juice, brought to your table hot from the broiler after a tender basting of wines and herbs
Half Broiled Chicken, Wild Rice - Half a partially boned chicken, carefully broiled and basted with wines and herbs, served on a bed of wild rice
New York Cut Steak
BROILED LAMB RIBS.  A Canlis' favorite for many years.  It is best to cut between each tiny rib and hold the morsel in your fingers - but no tastier lamb is to be found.  We give these ribs our matchless broiler treatment of herbs and wine, and offer them

Nelson's Blood (cocktail) Named for vice admiral Horatio Viscount Nelson, Britain's most famous Naval hero, who was mortally wounded at the Battle of Trafalgar on October 21st, 1805. Legend has it that his body was returned in a cask of Pusser's rum and that the sailors bore a hole in the cask to get at the rum, thereby drinking "Nelson's Blood". We celebrate this bit of liquid history by blending 3 ounces of Pusser's Rum with cranberry, orange and pineapple juice topped off with a big squeeze of West Indian Lime, nutmeg and cinnamon.
Sunburnt Senorita, glass Tequila Gold, Midori, passion fruit nectar, orange juice and grenadine.
Lady Hamilton (cocktail) A light and refeshing concoction which may have been the favorite of the lovely lady if she were still in these parts. In her honor, we pour in a tall glass. 1-1/2 Pusser's Rum, a squeeze of fresh lime juice and equal parts passion fruit, orange juice,and ginger ale.
Tequila Sunrise, glass Suaza Gold Tequila, orange juice and a dash of grenadine
Navy Grog-Nothing to do with the original drink, but our Navy Grog is a refeshing blend of 3-1/2 ounces of Pusser's Rum, fresh lime juice, pineapple juice, passion fruit nectar and a dash of Falernurn.
Fuzzy Naval (cocktail) Delicious, powerful and direct. We blend 1 ounce of Pusser's Rum, 2 ounces De Kuyper's Peachtree Schnapps and orange juice
John Courage Ale on Draft; glass; pitcher
Bloody Pusser's (cocktail)  The durable tomato juice treat, island style. 1-1/2 ounces of Pusser's Rum. served over the rocks, with lime juice, tomato juice and a touch of Tabasco and Worcestershire sauces

Can you use Chopsticks?
To fully enjoy your Oriental dinner, may we suggest the use of chopsticks.
Hold your rice bowl in the palm of one hand with the bowl serving as a "Napkin" as you enjoy your dinner with chopsticks.  Always keep the pointed ends of your chopsticks even.
As shown in figure "A," hold the first chopstick firmly in a stationary or fixed postion.
As shown in figure "B", the second chopstick is held like a pencil, using the thumb, index and second fingers.  Manipulate this chopstick to meet the first chopstick.
As shown in figure "C," this manipulating motion will form a vise to pick up your food.
